requirements.requirement: Run node1 as the writable PostgreSQL primary and node2/node3 as healthy read-only streaming standbys.
requirements.summary: Final observations show node1 out of recovery with transaction_read_only off, while both standbys are in recovery with read-only mode enabled. Both replication senders and physical slots are active and caught up, and real standby INSERT attempts are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Replicate committed changes from node1 to both standbys.
requirements.summary: A transaction committed on node1 after all restarts, and both node2 and node3 subsequently contained both committed probe rows while their WAL receivers remained streaming.

requirements.requirement: Carry PostgreSQL traffic over the dedicated database network and keep it off the management network.
requirements.summary: PostgreSQL listens only on the respective 10.100.211.10–12 database addresses. Observed replication sessions and directly connected routes use those addresses; port 5432 is not globally opened, and firewall/HBA access is restricted to database-network peers using certificate authentication.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent final-state and behavioral evidence. The primary is writable, both standbys are read-only and caught up, committed changes reach both, traffic is confined to the dedicated database addresses, and all three nodes recover correctly after independently verified restarts.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified, retained or reverted. Package installation, TLS credentials, PostgreSQL configuration, base backups, firewall rules, service enablement, and bounded probe data all directly supported implementation or verification. The malformed rich-rule attempts wrote configuration that became part of the final solution but did not show a successful firewall mutation; corrected rules immediately followed. Final snapshots show clean package health, no failed services, and only the intended address-specific PostgreSQL listeners. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete on every node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state, and a matching fixed after-executor boot identity.
